source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Zen Technologies' subsidiary Vector Technics became India's only company able to design and manufacture a fully integrated drone propulsion system in-house, 'eliminating dependence on Chinese components' — the company notes that ~80% of critical propulsion components used in India-manufactured drones are currently imported from China. Separately, Zen secured an export order worth over USD 41.5 million for military training and counter-UAS solutions in 2025, and FY25 exports reached roughly 37% of revenue. Framed as defense indigenization/self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) rather than an explicit customer-driven China+1 sourcing narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: Overwhelmingly government/defense-linked: customers include the Ministry of Defence, Indian armed forces, and police forces; '100+ government customers', '90% of orders from repeat clients'. Recent orders include a ₹295 crore MoD simulator order and a ₹289 crore counter-UAS upgrade order. No explicit revenue percentage disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export order worth over USD 41.5 million for military training/counter-UAS solutions (2025); FY25 exports approximately 37% of revenue, implying meaningful USD-denominated revenue. No explicit USD revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme participation found. Benefits from defense indigenization / Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat procurement preferences rather than a cash-incentive PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Commentary frames Netweb's growth against India's 'Make in India' and import-substitution push in HPC/servers: IndiaAI Mission's ~₹103 billion allocation over FY25-29 for domestic compute infrastructure, Make in India mandates, and National Supercomputing Mission 2.0's focus on indigenous systems. Risk-factor language notes reliance on NVIDIA/AMD/Intel for critical processors — supply still import-dependent rather than diversification away from China. Import-substitution/domestic-manufacturing framing rather than an explicit customer China+1 narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: Per Equitymaster's FY2024-25 Annual Report Analysis of Netweb Technologies: 'Government contributed 25.1% revenue vs non-Government 74.9%' (AI Systems deal classified as non-Government). Has also won government-linked sovereign AI compute infrastructure orders (e.g. a ₹558.8 crore strategic order) tied to national HPC/supercomputing missions.

inr_exposure.evidence: Sources critical processors/components internationally (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel; import records show shipments involving Super Micro Computer Inc., Taiwan), implying USD-denominated cost exposure on imports. Export revenue was about 9% of sales in Q3 FY25, with management guiding exports toward ~10% of sales within 2-3 years. No explicit USD revenue percentage or formal hedging policy disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Received an incentive of Rs 5.93-5.94 crore under the PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware, for the claim period July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024 (announced April 2025). Percentage of revenue attributable to PLI not disclosed.

rural.evidence: Distribution model noted for 'broad distribution footprint in urban and semi-urban regions', products reaching 'over 1,400 towns across the country' via the Nashik manufacturing facility and distribution network. No specific rural/semi-urban revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Third-party summary of GSK India's forex risk disclosure states currency fluctuations add forex risk for export earnings, though hedges mitigate some exposure.
inr_exposure.evidence: Imports vaccines/specialty medicines and, as a GSK plc subsidiary, likely pays royalties/technical fees to the GSK Group typically denominated in GBP/USD. No specific USD revenue percentage or formal hedging policy detail found; the AR PDF itself could not be fetched in this session.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed disclosure of participation in India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs. Broader scheme offers 10-20% incentives on incremental sales of 53 eligible APIs/KSMs/intermediates; GSK-specific participation could not be confirmed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Per coverage of Hitachi Energy India's Q3 FY25 results: 'Excluding the one-time large HVDC order, the share of exports grew to over 40 per cent of total orders in Q3 FY25, with power quality, substation & renewable orders from Australia, Indonesia, Canada, Croatia, and Azerbaijan, among others.' Order-inflow data (not revenue); reflects general export/global-diversification momentum rather than an explicit China+1 framing.

govt_capex.evidence: Order backlog reached a record ₹19,245.9 crore at FY25 year-end, driven substantially by a large HVDC order to transmit renewable energy from Khavda, Gujarat to Nagpur, Maharashtra. Also awarded an order to deliver 765 kV transformers to Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) 'to advance the country's grid expansion' (June 2025). Heavy dependence on government/PSU grid-infrastructure capex; no explicit revenue percentage disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Industry-level (not company-specific) analysis notes CRGO steel and copper together account for up to 70% of production costs in power transformer manufacturing, with copper prices swinging 25-30% annually; transformers also use petroleum-derived mineral insulating oil. No Hitachi Energy India-specific quantification found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Order book includes meaningful export orders (over 40% of order inflows ex-HVDC in Q3 FY25) to Australia, Indonesia, Canada, Croatia, and Azerbaijan, implying foreign-currency revenue exposure, alongside a ~₹4,000 crore capex program including a new greenfield large power transformer facility in Karjan, Vadodara. No explicit revenue-basis USD percentage or hedging policy disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed PLI scheme participation found. India's Power Secretary has floated a possible future PLI scheme for transmission equipment (e.g. CRGO steel localization), but no such scheme confirmed as active/benefiting Hitachi Energy India.

china_plus_one.evidence: China Plus One cited by analyst commentary as boosting export inquiries; management targets 20% export revenue by 2026, mid-teens export growth FY26-28 (lighting/acoustics to ASEAN/Europe).

rural.evidence: 2W rural sentiment recovery cited (+19% YoY) supporting Switching segment growth; no percentage disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Selected for PLI white-goods scheme (₹2,299cr committed investment); named among Auto PLI Component Champion beneficiaries from FY27.

china_plus_one.evidence: Described as well-positioned in China Plus One supply chain diversification via a new electrolyte-additives (battery chemicals) facility 'challenging Chinese supply-chain dominance'; exports rose to ~74% of net sales in FY25 (56% in FY24) across 55+ countries.

crude_exposure.evidence: Petrochemical-derived feedstocks likely but no percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~74% export revenue implies meaningful FX exposure; no explicit USD percentage or hedging policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: ECMS (government production-linked scheme, MeitY) approval for a ₹256.47cr electrolyte-additives project, ₹119.12cr eligible for up to 25% subsidy through FY2030-31. Note: this is ECMS, not the pharma Bulk-Drug/KSM PLI.

rural.evidence: Premiumisation trends described as 'playing out across both urban and emerging markets'; no rural percentage disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs are ENA/grain and glass, not crude-linked; ENA/grain guided 'stable to favourable' through FY26.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~9-10% of revenue (5-6% of volumes) to 100+ countries; short-term US tariff headwinds noted.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcoholic beverages not a PLI-covered sector.

china_plus_one.evidence: 'Strategic expansion in Europe and into EV-related products'; aftermarket exports +29%; European business +15.4% YoY (EBITDA +20.9%) — growth mentioned without an explicit China-diversification framing.

crude_exposure.evidence: Aluminium die-casting/rubber-polymer inputs have indirect crude linkage; no percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Italy-based European subsidiaries; European business +15.4% YoY implies EUR revenue exposure; no percentage or hedging policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not named among Auto PLI beneficiaries (list includes Toyota Kirloskar, Motherson Sumi, Bosch, Lucas-TVS).

ABB.report_year: CY2024 (ABB India follows Jan-Dec fiscal year; Integrated Annual Report 2024/2025)

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party coverage describes India as an 'export hub to support other geographies', with the CEO citing India becoming ABB's third-largest market and continued investment (~$75m planned for 2026, >$230m over the past decade) in expanding local manufacturing/R&D. Export/diversification momentum, but no explicit AR quote framing it as China+1-driven revenue growth was located.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources report exports account for 'only 10% of the business mix', with the company operating primarily on a 'local for local' model (~85-90% of products designed/manufactured and sold domestically); India also contributes ~10-11% of ABB Group's global exports.

china_plus_one.evidence: Broker research notes the share of three key export customers (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion) rose to ~80% of exports in 1HFY26 from 63% in FY24, and that the company has worked to de-risk fluorspar supply via long-term contracts with South African miners given China's dominance of global fluorspar supply — an input-side de-risking narrative rather than an explicit AR-stated China+1 export-demand narrative.

crude_exposure.evidence: Sources note dependence on imported raw materials like fluorspar and energy prices which can impact margins; a ~100bps gross margin dip from rising raw material costs in FY25. Fluorspar is a mined mineral rather than a crude-oil derivative, so no clear crude-oil-linked cost exposure confirmed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Broker notes cite 'a solid export contribution of 77% in Q4FY25', with major exports (specialty fluorochemicals, CDMO/CRAMS) billed to global agrochemical/pharma majors presumably in USD/EUR; this is quarter-specific (Q4FY25) rather than a confirmed full-year revenue split.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found linking to a PLI scheme beneficiary list; specialty chemicals/CDMO growth appears driven by customer contracts rather than disclosed PLI incentives.

china_plus_one.evidence: Vertically integrated defence & aerospace electronics supplier to Indian DRDO/armed forces (LCA-Tejas, BrahMos, LUH, etc.); export orders were only ~Rs 78 crore (~12% of the order book) in FY25, growth explicitly attributed to the Indian government's domestic 'Make in India' defence indigenisation push rather than a China+1 export/supply-chain-diversification narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: 'Growth prospects remain healthy, driven by the Indian Government's focus on indigenisation in the defence sector as part of the Make in India programme', with India's FY25 defence budget cited at ~Rs 6.2 lakh crore. Revenue is overwhelmingly domestic and defence/government-contract-driven (DRDO, armed forces programs); no specific revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export orders of ~Rs 78 crore representing ~12% of the order book in FY25 — an order-book proxy rather than a confirmed revenue-based export split; no hedging policy disclosure located.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found confirming status as a listed beneficiary of the electronics/IT-hardware PLI scheme; growth attributed generally to Make in India defence indigenisation policy rather than a confirmed PLI incentive.

china_plus_one.evidence: Described as heavily export-oriented, with export order inflow of Rs 1,733 crore (up 76% YoY) out of total order inflow of Rs 2,238 crore (up 51%) in FY25, a global footprint of 6,300+ generators installed across 100+ countries, and growing market share in the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia alongside partnerships with global turbine OEMs/EPCs. Strong export/diversification momentum but no explicit 'China+1' framing found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Described as maintaining a conservative debt profile, with an average debt to EBITDA ratio of just 0.32 and net debt to equity effectively at zero, funding growth via retained earnings/internal cash flows rather than debt — implying low exposure to interest-rate/floating-debt risk, though no specific floating-rate liability percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export order inflow and turnover figures across recent quarters/years range from ~67% to ~79% depending on period (e.g. export order inflow 76% of total order inflow growth in FY25), reflecting a heavily USD/foreign-currency-exposed revenue base sold across 70+ countries. No explicit hedging policy disclosure located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst commentary indicates CDMOs including Divi's Laboratories are reporting a significant increase in RFQs from global pharma majors looking to de-risk supply chains from China, and India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs is expected to reduce API dependence on China by 25-30% over 4-5 years. Not independently confirmed as verbatim AR MD&A language since the AR PDF could not be fetched directly.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Reported as entirely debt-free, implying minimal-to-no exposure to floating-rate interest liabilities.

crude_exposure.evidence: Management commentary (earnings calls) notes solvent and key-starting-material costs rose sharply, some prices doubling/tripling, exacerbated by geopolitical tensions in West Asia (petroleum-linked solvents). No explicit percentage of raw material cost tied to crude disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (~87% of gross sales in most recent confirmed full year, skewed toward Europe ~52% and North America ~17%) imply substantial foreign-currency revenue, but a USD-specific breakout and formal hedging policy were not confirmed.

govt_capex.evidence: EIL (a Navratna PSU) secured an all-time-high order inflow of Rs 8,214 crore in FY25 (up 141% YoY), driven by large capex announcements from oil-marketing-company (OMC) PSU clients; HPCL and associates alone account for ~33% of the outstanding ~Rs 11,700 crore order book. Demand-side, not raw-material-cost, linkage.

inr_exposure.evidence: Some USD-denominated overseas consultancy revenue, including a USD 350 million Dangote refinery expansion project in Nigeria, but overall percentage of total revenue in USD not disclosed.

rural.evidence: FY25 domestic tile demand was described as muted overall (industry volumes roughly flat), with branded players continuing to expand distribution/showroom networks into tier-2/tier-3 towns to gain share from unorganized players (organized sector share ~46% in FY25, projected to reach ~55% by FY29).
